external_deps: llama.cpp or another OpenAI-compatible inference server

review.tagline: Go proxy that starts and swaps local inference servers per request
review.summary: llama-swap is a single Go binary that sits in front of local inference servers such as llama.cpp, vllm, stable-diffusion.cpp and audio.cpp. It reads the `model` field of each OpenAI- or Anthropic-style request, starts the matching server from a YAML `cmd`, and stops the previous one. It includes a web UI, API keys, TTL unloading and a matrix DSL for running models concurrently.
review.audience: Self-hosters running several local models on one machine behind one API
strengths: One binary and one YAML file, no external dependencies
Works with any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible upstream server, not only llama.cpp
Matrix DSL runs chosen models concurrently; ttl unloads idle ones
Built-in web UI with playground, token metrics, log streaming and Prometheus /metrics
weaknesses: Does not run inference itself; you supply and configure the upstream servers
Originally designed for llama-server; Python servers like vllm should run in Docker or Podman
Swapping reloads the model, so the first request after a switch is slow
Auth is limited to API keys; no user accounts mentioned
needs: Needs llama.cpp or another OpenAI-compatible inference server
Models: GGUF via llama.cpp, vllm, stable-diffusion.cpp, whisper.cpp, audio.cpp
